title: Measurement of Aggregate Cohesion by Tissue Surface Tensiometry
protocol: Grow near-confluent adherent cell cultures to approximately 90% confluence.
Rinse monolayers twice with PBS.
Incubate cells in 0.05% trypsin-1 mM EDTA at 37°C until they detach.
Stop trypsinization by adding complete medium and gently triturate the mixture until cells are in suspension.
Transfer cell suspension to a 15 ml conical tube.
Add 40 μl of a 10 mg/ml DNAse stock solution and incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Vortex briefly and centrifuge at 200 x g for 5 minutes.
Discard supernatant and wash cell pellet with complete tissue culture medium.
Repeat washing step once more.
Resuspend cells in 2 mls of complete tissue culture medium.
Count the cells using a hemacytometer or automated cell counter.
Adjust cell concentration to 2.5 x 10^6 cells/ml.
Prepare a hydration chamber by placing 5 ml of PBS in a 60 mm tissue culture dish and removing its lid.
Depose 10 μl drops onto the inverted lid using a 20 μl pipette, ensuring they are sufficiently apart to not touch.
Invert the lid onto the PBS-filled bottom chamber.
Incubate at 37°C/5% CO2/95% humidity.
Monitor the drops daily and incubate until cell sheets or aggregates have formed.
Transfer sheets to round-bottom glass shaker flasks containing 3 mls of complete medium once they form.
Incubate in a shaking water bath at 37°C and 5% CO2 until spheroids form.
Prepare single cell suspensions adjusted to 1x10^6 cells/ml.
Transfer 3 ml of the cell suspension to 10 ml round-bottom flasks.
Incubate flasks in a gyratory water bath/shaker at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 4h at 120 rpm until cells recover from trypsinization.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 200 X g into a thin pellet.
Incubate the pellet for another 24 h until a coherent sheet forms.
Dislodge the sheet by gently swirling the culture tube.
Pour the contents of the culture tube into a small, sterile glass tissue culture dish.
Use micro scalpels to cut the sheets into fragments of various sizes.
Incubate fragments at 37°C on the gyratory waterbath shaker at 120 rpm under 5% CO2 for 2 to 3 days or until they become spherical.
Position the cell aggregate on the lower compression plate in the inner chamber of the tissue surface tensiometer.
Raise the central core until it contacts and compresses the cell aggregate.
Connect the upper compression plate to the balance arm by a flame-straightened nickel-chromium wire.
Adjust the central core position to control the distance between the parallel plates, initiating compression of the aggregate.
Hang a 15-inch length of wire from a retort stand and clamp a small binder clip to the end.
Run a Bunsen burner up and down the length of the wire until it glows red.
Cut the straightened wire into appropriate lengths.
Bend the wire approximately ¼ inch from the end using two razor blades to form a small hook.
Insert one end of the bent wire into the barrel of the lower compression plate.
Fill the inner chamber with pre-warmed CO2-independent tissue culture medium.
Position aggregates ranging in size from about 200-300 μm on the lower compression plate.
Aspirate an aggregate in tissue culture medium half-way up the tip of a Pasteur pipette fitted with a silicone bulb.
Transfer the pipette to the inner chamber and position the tip above the lower compression plate (LCP).
Gently expel the aggregate onto the LCP by gently squeezing the bulb or allow it to fall by gravity.
Position the upper compression plate (UCP) above the aggregate and allow it to settle, establishing a pre-compression apparent UCP weight baseline.
Raise the LCP until the aggregate is compressed against the UCP.
Adjust the height of the inner core of the lower apparatus to control different degrees of compression.
Monitor compression by observation through a dissecting microscope equipped with a CCD video camera.
Capture aggregate images and digitize them using ImageJ.
Continuously record apparent UCP weight change on a strip chart recorder.
Achievement of shape equilibrium is denoted by leveling-off of the Cahn balance's voltage output.
Subject each aggregate to 2 different degrees of compression.
Calculate aggregate surface tension.
At shape equilibrium, measure the compressive force acting on an aggregate of cells compressed between parallel plates.
Determine the radius of the equator (R2) of the compressed aggregate.
Measure the radius of an arc (R3) defining the surface profile normal to the compressing plates and extending between them.
Calculate the area of the surface of the aggregate upon which force F is exerted using πr³/2.
Apply measurements to the Young-Laplace equation to generate numerical values of apparent tissue surface tension.
Upon reaching equilibrium, decompress aggregates and allow them to approach a second equilibrium.
Measure compressive force and geometry at the new shape equilibrium.
Calculate σ2 as described above for the second equilibrium state.
